items.title: Subpolynomial query complexity for log-concave sampling

review.scope: Manuscript introduction and pinned upstream Model/Main: complete model, quantifiers, conditional rescaling, attributed mechanism comparison and literal displayed Lean. Pin membership verified independently through GitHub contents API.
review.accepted_boundary: No local Lean compilation, exhaustive source-proof coverage, mathematical priority or complete source-equivalence certificate is claimed.

reader.source_anchor: eq:original-class; thm:main; Historical context; Proof strategy and principal ingredients
reader.question: At fixed conditioning and fixed TV accuracy, must a sampler pay a positive power of dimension in exact first-order queries?
reader.takeaway: The source claims that every fixed positive dimension exponent can be achieved in this oracle model. It does not give a polylogarithmic bound or an efficient arithmetic implementation.
reader.model: For d >= 2, V is C2, the supplied minimizer is zero, V(0)=0, and the Hessian bounds hold everywhere. A query returns both V(x) and its gradient. Algorithms are measurable, adaptive and randomized; computation between queries is unrestricted. Their only information about V comes from oracle replies. One algorithm for each d must work uniformly over the potential class, with a query cap on every run, not only in expectation.
reader.statement: Let Q(d) be the least deterministic query budget of a uniform sampler whose output is within TV 1/10 of every admissible Gibbs law. For each epsilon > 0 there is a finite C_epsilon giving the upper bound below for all d >= 2. There are absolute c > 0 and d0 giving the independent lower bound for every d >= d0. The optimal dimension exponent is zero. Epsilon is exponent slack, not output error; TV accuracy remains 1/10.
reader.statement_formula: \begin{aligned}\forall\varepsilon>0\;\exists C_\varepsilon<\infty\;\forall d\ge2:&\quad Q(d)\le C_\varepsilon d^\varepsilon,\\\exists c>0,d_0\;\forall d\ge d_0:&\quad Q(d)\ge c\log d,\\&\quad\gamma_*=0.\end{aligned}
reader.source_comparison: The manuscript identifies smoothed Picard HMC as a methodological precedent: Gaussian density smoothing, conditional cumulants and high-order Picard approximation already occur there. It also identifies proximal conditional sampling and rotational/Krylov lower-bound arguments as prior frameworks. Its claimed extra work is the all-split tensor control and finite implementation of nested noisy conditional means, followed by removal of auxiliary noise. This is the manuscript's comparison; an independent literature/priority audit remains pending.
reader.source_comparison_boundary: Do not compare a W2 guarantee to TV without an actual conversion. Expected-query bounds need a uniform tail/cap argument before comparison to this every-run model. The source attributes the logarithmic lower-bound strategy to prior work: that part is not advertised here as a new mathematical principle.

steps.title: Make the conditional problem almost Gaussian
steps.text: Add independent Gaussian noise of variance h > 0 to a target sample. The conditional density at a fixed noisy observation y contains a Gaussian quadratic plus V. Substitute x=y+sqrt(h) z: its Jacobian is constant in z and cancels in normalization. Writing F_y(z)=V(y+sqrt(h) z), the chain rule gives grad F_y(z)=sqrt(h) grad V(y+sqrt(h) z). Therefore beta=2 implies Lip(grad F_y) <= 2h. Each evaluation needs one original gradient query; no higher derivative oracle was introduced.
steps.formula: p_y(x)\propto e^{-V(x)-\|x-y\|^2/(2h)},\qquad p_y^Z(z)\propto e^{-\|z\|^2/2-F_y(z)},\qquad\|\nabla F_y(z)-\nabla F_y(w)\|\le2h\|z-w\|.
steps.boundary: A genuine conditional-kernel identification still needs normalization, joint measurability and the a.e. conditional-version argument. This displayed calculation is not an admitted local kernel theorem.

steps.title: Reduce sampling and high derivatives to conditional means
steps.text: For 0 <= rho <= 1, interpolate a near-Gaussian sample with independent Gaussian noise. The source expresses the marginal velocity through a conditional gradient mean. At positive Gaussian smoothing scales, conditioning supplies higher derivatives even though the original potential is only C2; no arbitrary smoothness is inferred at an unsmoothed endpoint. All-split tensor estimates control the contractions used by the flow, avoiding a new dimension factor at every derivative order.
steps.formula: Y_\rho=\rho Z+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}N,\qquad N\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d)\text{ independent of }Z.
steps.boundary: The velocity identity, tensor norm conventions and estimates are separate source obligations, not conclusions of the interpolation formula.

steps.title: Turn the conditional mean into a noisy output
steps.text: A skew-matrix drift preserves a product of the smoothed marginal and Gaussian momentum. Its momentum displacement converts an integral of conditional gradient means into a Gaussian centered at the requested mean. The derivative bounds are then used in discretizing this flow.
steps.boundary: Skewness alone does not prove invariance: domains, integrability, flow semantics and the product-law argument remain to be discharged.

steps.title: Implement nested means with actual queries
steps.text: Polynomial/Picard expressions use exact conditional means at centers that are themselves produced recursively. A pathwise seed translation leaves primitive query locations unchanged when the center shifts; a covariance reduction absorbs center noise. The source separately bounds expression dependency depth and routine-call height before selecting error budgets and meshes.
steps.boundary: This exact seed/covariance mechanism is a candidate source contribution, not an assumed noisy-mean oracle. Proving termination and an every-run query cap is part of the formalization.

steps.title: Return from auxiliary laws to the actual target
steps.text: The proximal chain first supplies a noised target. Repeated conditioning halves the remaining variance; a mode-centered Gaussian handles the final small-noise problem. The accuracy obligation is for the unnoised Gibbs law, so the noise-removal argument cannot be deleted from the upper route.
steps.boundary: Contraction, error accumulation and deterministic query accounting remain separate from merely writing a proximal update.

steps.title: Keep the information lower bound independent
steps.text: The separate lower route uses rotational/Krylov information, an explicit spectrum and a separating statistic. Its source statement covers arbitrary randomized adaptive algorithms and unrestricted randomized outputs at the same fixed TV threshold.
steps.boundary: The lower bound does not say that the upper algorithm is logarithmic, and an upper-route lemma does not prove any lower-bound obligation.

reader.assembly: The upstream main theorem joins three already named providers: the subpolynomial upper bound, the independent logarithmic lower bound, and the exponent identity. The short final Lean proof is an assembly step; all algorithm, analytic and information-theoretic work lives in its providers. ASTIS has not yet admitted that source-specific closure.
reader.lean_statement:
theorem exact_source_main :
    (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ d : ℕ, 2 ≤ d →
      (queryComplexity d).toENNReal ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * (d : ℝ) ^ ε)) ∧
    (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ d₀ : ℕ, 2 ≤ d₀ ∧ ∀ d : ℕ, d₀ ≤ d →
      ENNReal.ofReal (c * Real.log (d : ℝ)) ≤ (queryComplexity d).toENNReal) ∧
    gammaStar = 0
reader.lean_explanation: The conjunction symbol separates three obligations. The upper quantifiers let the constant depend on exponent slack but not dimension or the potential. The lower bound has its own positive constant and dimension threshold. queryComplexity uses extended natural numbers; gammaStar is defined through exponent bounds. The three names in the proof are upstream providers, not callable ASTIS declarations.
reader.next_boundary: Before porting: audit Model.Admissible, OracleAlgorithm.history/run, CanSample and queryComplexity; compare the literal potential, Gibbs, measurability and query semantics with canonical ASTIS. Then choose one substantive dependency-ready edge from the actual source closure. No local producer or adapter is inferred from chapter placement.
